geo.title: What to know
geo.body:
Targeted stations.

Goal: I can close gaps from the assessment.

  • 2.1 I can justify algebra steps with properties of equality.
  • 2.2 I can use the Ruler Postulate and segment addition.
  • 2.3 I can find a midpoint on a number line and in the coordinate plane.
  • 2.4 I can use the Protractor Postulate and angle addition.
  • 2.5 I can construct a segment bisector and an angle bisector and give an informal reason why they work (formal proof in 4.13).
  • 2.6 I can prove that complements (supplements) of the same angle are equal.
  • 2.7 I can prove vertical angles are equal.
  • 2.8 I can prove that perpendicular lines form four right angles.
  • 2.9 I can construct a perpendicular through a point on and off a line.
  • 2.10 I can copy an angle and use it to construct a parallel line, with informal reasoning (copying justified in 4.13, parallel test proved in 5.6).
  • 2.11 I can write a two-column or flow chart proof about angles.
  • 2.12 I can combine constructions into a design and explain each step.

slides.title: Practice: 2.1
slides.html: Which property justifies: If m angle 1 = m angle 2 and m angle 2 = 40, then m angle 1 = 40?
slides.reveal: The transitive property of equality (substitution also works).

slides.title: Practice: 2.7
slides.html: Two lines cross and one angle is 47 degrees. Find the other three.
slides.reveal: Its vertical angle is 47; the other two are 180 − 47 = 133 degrees each.

slides.title: Practice: 2.10
slides.html: Which angles are made equal when you build a parallel this way?
slides.reveal: A pair of corresponding angles formed by the crossing line (the transversal) with l and with the new line.

slides.title: Common traps
slides.html:
Watch out for these common mistakes:

  • congruent and equal are interchangeable in every context
  • vertical angles are any angles "across"
  • a perpendicular bisector is any perpendicular line
  • a construction is the same as a drawing measured with a ruler
